seoDescription: Die cut waterproof stickers on laminated vinyl or BOPP, cut to your artwork outline for bottles, coolers, helmets and kayaks. Free proof, free US shipping.
tagline: Laminated vinyl cut to the outline of your design, built to shrug off sinks, rain, sweat and dishwashers.
quickAnswer: Die cut waterproof stickers are printed on white or clear vinyl, sealed under a gloss or matte laminate, then cut to the outline of the artwork so no square background surrounds the design. The film does not absorb water and the adhesive holds through washing and rain. They suit water bottles, coolers, helmets, kayaks and outdoor gear. From $0.30 per sticker, 100 minimum, 5 to 7 business days production.

sections.h2: Are die cut stickers waterproof? Only when all three layers are
sections.html:
A die cut sticker is waterproof when the film, the ink and the adhesive each handle water on their own. Paper fails at the first layer, so a paper sticker cut to a beautiful shape still wrinkles in the sink. Vinyl or BOPP film fails at none of them as long as the ink is sealed under a laminate. That is the build on this page: white or clear vinyl, full-color print, laminate, then a cut that follows the artwork outline with a border of about 0.0625 inches. Each sticker comes as its own piece on a paper backing, not on a sheet.

The nearest sibling is our waterproof stickers page, which is the material page for every format: circles and rectangles, kiss cut sheets, rolls for a label applicator and shape-cut pieces. If you label a product line or want sheets of mixed designs, the waterproof sticker material page is the right place. This page is for the shape-cut version only, where the sticker is a logo, a mascot or a word with nothing around it, and where the cut edge meets water on every side.

sections.h2: Why the shape matters more once the sticker gets wet
sections.html:
Water finds the edge first. A square sticker has four straight edges and four corners. A die cut piece can have dozens of corners, tails and inside curves, and each one is a place where a fingernail, a dish brush or a jet of water can start a lift. The film and adhesive are the same as on a square, so the fix is in the artwork, not the material.

  • Round every outside corner to at least a 0.0625 inch radius; sharp points lift first and collect grime once they do
  • Avoid spikes, antlers and thin tails narrower than 0.125 inches, or let us add a small bridge of film behind them
  • Keep letters joined by a backing shape rather than cutting each one free, so a word is one piece with one edge
  • Add a printed border in a brand color if the design is mostly thin line art; it gives the cut a solid path to follow
  • Keep holes inside the design to 0.25 inches or more; smaller inside cuts trap water and soap

Lamination goes on before cutting, so the laminate and film are trimmed together and the ink stays sealed between them right to the edge. Nothing wicks in from the side.

sections.h2: Wet conditions and which waterproof build handles them
sections.html:
Vinyl is the default for gear and vehicles. BOPP is a thinner film that suits jars and bottles where the sticker wraps a curve and is handled rather than scrubbed. Clear vinyl carries a white ink layer under the colors so they stay solid on glass. sections.h2: Applying a die cut waterproof sticker so it stays put
sections.html:
Most waterproof stickers that fail were applied wrong, not made wrong. The order below takes two minutes and is the difference between a sticker that lasts a season and one that lasts years.

  1. Wipe the surface with isopropyl alcohol on a lint-free cloth. Skip soap; it leaves a film the adhesive cannot bond through.
  2. Let the surface dry fully and come to room temperature. A bottle straight from the fridge sweats, and the sticker goes on wet.
  3. Peel the backing, hold the sticker by its edges, set the center down first and press outward with a card.
  4. Run a thumbnail around the entire edge, paying attention to corners and tails, which are where lifting starts.
  5. Wait 24 hours before any water, and 72 hours before a dishwasher or a pressure washer.

Never apply underwater or to a wet surface. The adhesive is pressure sensitive and needs dry contact to bond; once it has bonded, water cannot get between it and the surface.

sections.h2: Waterproof, reflective, all-weather: pick the right word for the job
sections.html:
Waterproof says what the sticker survives, not where it belongs. A waterproof die cut sticker on a shaded wall will last for years; the same sticker on a dashboard in Phoenix will fade in two, not because of water but because of ultraviolet light and 150 degree heat. If the job is outdoor and sun-facing, say so on the quote, and we will specify a thicker vinyl and a UV laminate for it. If the job is night visibility on a trailer or a helmet, waterproof is only half the answer; our custom reflective sticker page uses a film that bounces headlights back and happens to be waterproof as well.

Removable adhesive is available on waterproof vinyl for rental gear and seasonal windows, but it loosens faster in wet use than permanent. For anything washed daily, order permanent.

faqs.a: Only if they are printed on a film rather than paper and the ink is sealed under a laminate. Our die cut waterproof stickers use vinyl or BOPP with a gloss or matte laminate, so water cannot soak the stock, run the ink or float the adhesive. A die cut paper sticker is not waterproof no matter how it is cut.

faqs.q: Are die cut vinyl stickers waterproof without a laminate?
faqs.a: The vinyl itself is, but the ink on top is not fully protected. Unlaminated vinyl survives rain and a wipe-down, yet repeated scrubbing, dish brushes and sunscreen will wear the print. Every sticker on this page ships laminated, which is what makes it safe for sinks, dishwashers and daily handling.

faqs.q: Do the cut edges of a die cut waterproof sticker let water in?
faqs.a: No. The laminate is applied over the printed vinyl before the cutting step, so the two layers are trimmed together and the ink stays sandwiched between them right up to the edge. Vinyl does not wick, so there is no path for water. Edge lifting only happens when a corner was never pressed down properly.

faqs.q: Can die cut waterproof stickers go on a kayak or a paddleboard?
faqs.a: Yes, on the smooth polyethylene hull of a kayak and on the epoxy deck of a paddleboard. Clean with alcohol, apply dry, and give it 72 hours before the first launch. Rinse with fresh water after salt use, as you would the boat. Avoid the textured grip pad; the adhesive cannot bond to the texture.

faqs.q: Will die cut waterproof stickers stay on a helmet that gets sweaty?
faqs.a: Yes. Sweat, sunscreen and rain are what the laminate and acrylic adhesive are designed for. Apply to a clean, dry shell, keep the sticker under about 3 inches wide so it follows the curve without stress at the edges, and give it 24 hours before the first ride. Rounded corners on the design help on a curved surface.

faqs.q: Can I put die cut waterproof stickers on a cooler lid that sits in the sun?
faqs.a: Yes, and on a hard cooler they last for years. Tell us the cooler lives outdoors so we laminate for UV as well as water. Rotomolded lids are smooth and bond well; the one spot to avoid is the rubber gasket area. A sticker on a soft cooler fabric will peel, so stick to the hard sides.

faqs.q: Do die cut waterproof stickers work on a chilled bottle straight from the fridge?
faqs.a: Not at the moment of application. A cold bottle sweats, and a sticker pressed onto condensation never bonds. Let the bottle come to room temperature, wipe it dry, apply the sticker, and give it 24 hours. After that, the fridge, condensation and ice buckets are no problem for the life of the bottle.

faqs.q: What happens to a die cut waterproof sticker in a pressure washer?
faqs.a: After a 72 hour cure, it stays put under a normal car wash or a pressure washer held a foot or more away. A high-pressure jet aimed straight at an edge from a few inches can lift a corner, and once a corner is up, dirt gets under it. Wash across the sticker, not into its edges.

faqs.q: Does a matte laminate make a die cut waterproof sticker less waterproof?
faqs.a: No. Gloss and matte laminates are the same film with a different surface texture, and both seal the ink completely. Matte reduces glare and looks softer on packaging; gloss makes colors deeper and wipes cleaner. Pick on looks and where the sticker will be photographed, not on water resistance.

faqs.q: How many die cut waterproof stickers do I have to order?
faqs.a: The minimum is 100 per design. Prices start from $0.30 per sticker and rise with size, lamination and quantity, so a 2 inch bottle sticker at 500 pieces costs much less per piece than a 6 inch cooler decal at 100. Several sizes of the same artwork can be combined to reach the 100.

faqs.q: Can I write on a die cut waterproof sticker with a marker?
faqs.a: A permanent marker writes on gloss laminate and stays, though it can be wiped off with alcohol. Pen and pencil will not take on either laminate because the surface is sealed. If you need a label that staff fill in by hand, ask for a matte laminate with a printed write-on panel, or consider a paper sticker for dry indoor use.

faqs.q: How long do die cut waterproof stickers take to produce and ship?
faqs.a: Production takes 5 to 7 business days after you approve the free digital proof, and FedEx delivery inside the United States is free, so the usual total is 8 to 10 business days. Lamination is part of the standard run and does not add time. Ask about rush production on the quote if you have a fixed date.
